messages.subject: Re: Anyway to create an instance of uploaded file ?
parts:
Use "reactiveValues".  E.g.
Dat <- reactiveValues()
observe({
  Dat$data <- read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
})


output$venn <- renderPlot({
                venn(Dat$data)
                })

      output$table <- renderTable({
                as.data.frame(Dat$data)
                })


On Wednesday, May 21, 2014 11:29:01 PM UTC+2, Senthil Kumar wrote:
Hi shiny experts,

I am trying to develop an app, where user can upload input file, get venn diagram and a data table via tabsets (venn diagram in a tab and data table in another). As I want to render plot as well as table, I use 2 instances for reading the uploaded file. For example, my server.R will look something like 

shinyServer(function(input, output) {
      
     ##somestuff here

     readFile <- reactive({
inFile <- input$file1
if (is.null(inFile)){return(NULL)}
read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$sep, quote=input$quote)
})

      output$venn <- renderPlot({
                data <- readFile()
                ## some other stuff for filtration
                venn(filtered_data)
                })

      output$table <- renderTable({
                data <- readFile()
                ## some other stuff for filtration
                as.data.frame(filtered_data)
                })

As you can see, my concern is I am calling readFile() twice i.e. reading file twice even though I am doing same stuff both time except displaying 2 different things. It would make the app slower for bigger files. So if anyone can help/explain me if there is a way to create a 'read file' instance and pass it to renderPlot or renderTable. Any other idea is also completely welcome :)

Thanks a bunch in advance and also sorry if it is a silly question.

P.S: I cannot hard code reading file before 'shinyServer(function){}' as input file will obviously change according to users.

/Senthil
